g_policy.reason: The user opts in by choosing to play. The offer copy states the reward (priority routing, 60 minutes), declining leaves replies as they are, and the ad-fail path is defined.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of queue priority, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event: returning from the Upgrade entry without subscribing, then opening a chat. It does not use anything the user typed or said.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed or capped. The reward is a temporary boost on top of the free experience.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is 'Inside the character's reply', so the offer is sent as a message in the conversation. The failure path also adds 'a note in the chat', which is a system note in the chat. Both fall under the offer being inside the conversation itself.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Priority routing is sold as a Janitor+ benefit (l02, s02.e06), so the app charges for the resource this reward gives.

c2_evidence.reason: The proposal relies on free users waiting in a 'normal queue' and on a chat reply screen. The free-tier limit is an open question, m03 is only inferred, and no chat screen is in the model. The claim that a user 'came back from' the Upgrade entry is also not backed by any observed mechanic.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is a 60-minute sample of priority routing, capped at 2 per day. Longer memory, more swipes and the badge stay behind the subscription.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears just after a character reply is finished, which counts as a finished action, and the user can ignore it and keep chatting.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn unit. The reward is granted only after the verified play, and the trigger is a detectable app event.

c7_specific.reason: It names the Janitor+ priority routing benefit, the profile menu Upgrade entry, and My Chats, so it could not be moved to another app unchanged.

other_concern: An offer tied to having just visited the Upgrade entry is a confusing trigger, and the app may not be able to detect a user leaving that entry without subscribing. A sheet or dialog opened by an app event, such as a tap on a locked or priority item, would be a safer placement.
